passages.text: When the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought spices so they could go and anoint the body of Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Mary Magdalene was a follower of Jesus.
Mary, the mother of James, was also a follower of Jesus.
Salome was with them.
The Sabbath ended.
Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome acted together.
They bought spices.
They wanted to go to the tomb.
They planned to anoint the body of Jesus with the spices.
passages.original: Καὶ διαγενομένου τοῦ σαββάτου Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ Σαλώμη ἠγόρασαν ἀρώματα ἵνα ἐλθοῦσαι ἀλείψωσιν αὐτόν

passages.text: Very early on the first day of the week, just after sunrise, they went to the tomb.
passages.sermon:
Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome went to the tomb.
They went very early in the morning.
It was the first day of the week.
The sun had just risen.
passages.original: καὶ λίαν πρωῒ τῇ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ἔρχονται ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον ἀνατείλαντος τοῦ ἡλίου

passages.text: They were asking one another, “Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?”
passages.sermon:
Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome went to the tomb of Jesus.
They spoke to each other.
They asked a question.
They said, “Who will roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb?”
passages.original: καὶ ἔλεγον πρὸς ἑαυτάς Τίς ἀποκυλίσει ἡμῖν τὸν λίθον ἐκ τῆς θύρας τοῦ μνημείου

passages.text: But when they looked up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, even though it was extremely large.
passages.sermon:
The women went to the tomb of Jesus.
They looked up.
They saw the stone was rolled away from the entrance.
The stone was very large.
passages.original: καὶ ἀναβλέψασαι θεωροῦσιν ὅτι ἀποκεκύλισται ὁ λίθος ἦν γὰρ μέγας σφόδρα

passages.text: When they entered the tomb, they saw a young man dressed in a white robe sitting on the right side, and they were alarmed.
passages.sermon:
The women entered the tomb.
They saw a young man.
He sat on the right side.
He wore a white robe.
The women felt alarmed.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰσελθοῦσαι εἰς τὸ μνημεῖον εἶδον νεανίσκον καθήμενον ἐν τοῖς δεξιοῖς περιβεβλημένον στολὴν λευκήν καὶ ἐξεθαμβήθησαν

passages.text: But he said to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen! He is not here! See the place where they put Him.
passages.sermon:
A young man sat on the right side inside the tomb.
He wore a white robe.
He spoke to the women.
He said, “Do not be alarmed.
You are looking for Jesus from Nazareth.
He was crucified.
He has risen.
He is not here.
Look at the place where they put Him.”
passages.original: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐταῖς Μὴ ἐκθαμβεῖσθε Ἰησοῦν ζητεῖτε τὸν Ναζαρηνὸν τὸν ἐσταυρωμένον ἠγέρθη οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε ἴδε ὁ τόπος ὅπου ἔθηκαν αὐτόν

passages.text: But go, tell His disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee. There you will see Him, just as He told you.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The young man in the white robe spoke to the women at the tomb.
He told them to go.
He told them to tell Jesus’ disciples and Peter.
He said, “Jesus is going ahead of you into Galilee.”
He said, “You will see Him there.”
He said, “He told you this before.”
passages.original: ἀλλὰ ὑπάγετε εἴπατε τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ τῷ Πέτρῳ ὅτι Προάγει ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν ἐκεῖ αὐτὸν ὄψεσθε καθὼς εἶπεν ὑμῖν

passages.text: So the women left the tomb and ran away, trembling and bewildered. And in their fear they did not say a word to anyone.
passages.sermon:
The women left the tomb.
They ran away from the tomb.
They felt afraid.
They trembled.
They were confused.
They did not speak to anyone.
They stayed silent because they were afraid.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθοῦσαι ἔφυγον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου εἶχεν γὰρ αὐτὰς τρόμος καὶ ἔκστασις καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν εἶπαν ἐφοβοῦντο γάρ

passages.text: Early on the first day of the week, after Jesus had risen, He appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom He had driven out seven demons.
passages.sermon: Jesus rose from the dead early on the first day of the week.\r\nJesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene.\r\nJesus had driven seven demons out of Mary Magdalene.
passages.original: Ἀναστὰς δὲ πρωῒ πρώτῃ σαββάτου ἐφάνη πρῶτον Μαρίᾳ τῇ Μαγδαληνῇ παρ’ ἧς ἐκβεβλήκει ἑπτὰ δαιμόνια

passages.text: She went and told those who had been with Him, who were mourning and weeping.
passages.sermon:
Mary Magdalene saw Jesus alive.
Jesus had driven seven demons out of Mary Magdalene.
Mary Magdalene went to the people who had been with Jesus.
These people were mourning.
They were weeping.
Mary Magdalene told them what she had seen.
passages.original: ἐκείνη πορευθεῖσα ἀπήγγειλεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ γενομένοις πενθοῦσι καὶ κλαίουσιν

passages.text: And when they heard that Jesus was alive and she had seen Him, they did not believe it.
passages.sermon: The disciples heard that Jesus was alive.\r\nThey heard that Mary Magdalene had seen Him.\r\nThey did not believe this news.
passages.original: κἀκεῖνοι ἀκούσαντες ὅτι ζῇ καὶ ἐθεάθη ὑπ’ αὐτῆς ἠπίστησαν

passages.text: After this, Jesus appeared in a different form to two of them as they walked along in the country.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had risen from the dead.
Two of His followers walked in the country.
Jesus appeared to these two followers.
He showed Himself in a different form.
passages.original: Μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα δυσὶν ἐξ αὐτῶν περιπατοῦσιν ἐφανερώθη ἐν ἑτέρᾳ μορφῇ πορευομένοις εἰς ἀγρόν

passages.text: And they went back and reported it to the rest, but they did not believe them either.
passages.sermon:
Two of Jesus’ followers saw Him alive.
They went back to the other disciples.
They told the others what they had seen.
The other disciples did not believe them.
passages.original: κἀκεῖνοι ἀπελθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τοῖς λοιποῖς οὐδὲ ἐκείνοις ἐπίστευσαν

passages.text: Later, as they were eating, Jesus appeared to the Eleven and rebuked them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen Him after He had risen.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the risen Lord.
The Eleven disciples were eating together.
Jesus appeared to them.
He rebuked them.
He rebuked their unbelief.
He rebuked their hardness of heart.
They did not believe those who had seen Jesus alive after He had risen.
passages.original: Ὕστερον δὲ ἀνακειμένοις αὐτοῖς τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐφανερώθη καὶ ὠνείδισεν τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν καὶ σκληροκαρδίαν ὅτι τοῖς θεασαμένοις αὐτὸν ἐγηγερμένον οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν

passages.text: And He said to them, “Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Eleven disciples.
Jesus had risen from the dead.
Jesus said to them, "Go."
Go into all the world.
Preach the gospel.
Preach to every creature."
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Πορευθέντες εἰς τὸν κόσμον ἅπαντα κηρύξατε τὸ εὐαγγέλιον πάσῃ τῇ κτίσει

passages.text: Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Whoever believes will be saved.
Whoever is baptized will be saved.
Whoever does not believe will be condemned.”
passages.original: ὁ πιστεύσας καὶ βαπτισθεὶς σωθήσεται ὁ δὲ ἀπιστήσας κατακριθήσεται

passages.text: And these signs will accompany those who believe: In My name they will drive out demons; they will speak in new tongues; they will pick up snakes with their hands, and if they drink any deadly poison, it will not harm them; they will lay their hands on the sick, and they will be made well.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He described what would happen to those who believe in Him.
These signs will follow every believer.
Believers will act in the name of Jesus.
Believers will drive out demons.
Believers will speak in new languages.
Believers will pick up snakes with their hands.
If believers drink any deadly poison, it will not harm them.
Believers will lay their hands on sick people.
The sick will become well.
passages.original: σημεῖα δὲ τοῖς πιστεύσασιν ταῦτα παρακολουθήσει ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δαιμόνια ἐκβαλοῦσιν γλώσσαις λαλήσουσιν καιναῖς και ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν ὄφεις ἀροῦσιν κἂν θανάσιμόν τι πίωσιν οὐ μὴ αὐτοὺς βλάψῃ ἐπὶ ἀρρώστους χεῖρας ἐπιθήσουσιν καὶ καλῶς ἕξουσιν

passages.text: After the Lord Jesus had spoken to them, He was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
passages.sermon: The Lord Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nAfter He finished speaking, He was taken up into heaven.\r\nJesus sat down at the right hand of God.
passages.original: Ὁ μὲν οὖν Κύριος Ἰησοῦς μετὰ τὸ λαλῆσαι αὐτοῖς ἀνελήμφθη εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐκ δεξιῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: And they went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked through them, confirming His word by the signs that accompanied it.
passages.sermon:
The followers of Jesus went out.
They preached everywhere.
The Lord Jesus worked through them.
He confirmed His word.
He gave signs that accompanied their preaching.
passages.original: ἐκεῖνοι δὲ ἐξελθόντες ἐκήρυξαν πανταχοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου συνεργοῦντος καὶ τὸν λόγον βεβαιοῦντος διὰ τῶν ἐπακολουθούντων σημείων
